name: disgust
description: A strong aversion to something that could contaminate your physical, social, or existential well-being, but a sense that you can avoid it.
perceptions: This thing is ugly and unhealthy.
If I get too close it could stain or poison me somehow.

comparisons.description: 'Hate is not wanting to experience something, while 'disgust' is that plus a fear that the experience will somehow taint you with an impurity.

variations.name: physical disgust
variations.description: A strong aversion to a sight, smell, or thought of something that could make the body sick, along with a sense that you can avoid it.
perceptions: This thing is ugly, unhealthy, and/or smells bad.
If I get too close, it could make me sick.

guidance.description: Given how challenging it is to combat disgust, it might be helpful to instead focus on building disgust tolerance. Disgust tolerance means being able to stand the feeling and allowing it to pass. It is like a muscle that can be strengthened with practice. To build disgust tolerance, I recommend the following strategies: Pair disgust with something pleasant, Tie disgust tolerance with values, Talk it out, Be Open-Minded

variations.name: social disgust
variations.description: A strong negative reaction to someone breaking a social taboo.
perceptions: That is one of the worst social behaviors.
If I get too close, it could hurt my reputation.
I need to distance myself to avoid being contaminated.
results: signal your disapproval to distance yourself

guidance.description: If we empathize with the person who is disgusting us, we will not only do good for another, we will do good to ourselves and become undisgusted.

variations.name: existential disgust
variations.description: A strong aversion to something that is perceived to taint the purity of your soul.
perceptions: This thing could hurt my standing with God/Universe.
I need to distance myself to avoid being contaminated.
results: signal your disapproval to distance yourself

commentaries.quote: Disgust is underrated as a motivator. Perfectionists are just avoiding the stain of failure. The righteous are driven by the stink of cheating. Activists are reacting to behavior they deem rotten.

The more you read about the history of disgust, the more convinced you might be that it is the energy powering a whole host of seemingly unrelated phenomena, from our never-ending culture wars to the existence of kosher laws to 4chan to mermaids. Disgust is a bodily experience that creeps into every corner of our social lives, a piece of evolutionary hardware designed to protect our stomachs that expanded into a system for protecting our souls.
commentaries.attribution: Molly Young in How Disgust Explains Everything

commentaries.quote: Disgust is often more deeply buried than envy and anger, but it compounds and intensifies the other negative emotions.

Expect to be disgusted by your own early work. If writing is your vocation, if you hope that it might be your salvation, push on through the disgust until you find one true sentence, a few words that say more than you expected, something you didn't know until you set it down.

The emotion of disgust evolved initially to optimize responses to the omnivore's dilemma. Individuals who had a properly calibrated sense of disgust were able to consume more calories than their overly disgustable cousins while consuming fewer dangerous microbes than their insufficiently disgustable cousins.
commentaries.attribution: Jonathan Haidt, The Righteous Mind: Why Good People Are Divided by Politics and Religion

commentaries.quote: As an emotion, disgust is designed as a protection. When people feel disgusted, they tend to remove themselves from a situation.
